title: Fixed Battered Hollow Piles and Through Hatch Cap
description: One wholly newly authored complete fixed dry pile-cap foundation display inspired only by broad marine dolphin foundation vocabulary. Four entire thick-walled round tubular piles incline inward in two plan directions from four widely separated flat annular soles to four distinct full annular seats beneath one whole thick cap. Each pile is a true constant-radius tube about its inclined axis; both finished end planes are horizontal ellipses rather than uncropped oblique tube ends making edge-only support. Every pile retains its complete outer wall, continuous inner bore and both finite end rings as one closed material mesh. The complete upper cap has a broad bevelled eight-sided outer perimeter and one genuine central through-hatch; the central empty vertical shaft and full crosswise under-cap gaps remain open. The cap rests on four actual opposed finite annular patches; its solid material intentionally closes the top of each pile bore, while the four inspection-display lower bores remain open. Unlike the old two-metre timber pier tile, there is no plank deck, under-deck stringer, short vertical timber piling, collar or snapped shore module. All four hollow inclined tubes and the continuous ported cap were newly authored together as one whole structural appearance, not clipped from a dock, stool, roof, hull, old pile or old model. Five closed separately editable material meshes and three untextured opaque PBR roles, metre-style Z-up and four actual bottom annular contact patches. One model zero scenes. Deliberately bare dry foundation appearance: no bollard, fender, catwalk, railing, vessel, water, soil volume, reinforcement or operating berth. The exposed bottom cuts are an inspection datum, not piles supported safely on a seabed or claims of embedment. No dimensions or specification of any real project copied. No anchorage, soil resistance, pile driving, concrete/steel behaviour, buoyancy, impact, mooring, load rating, marine suitability, installation, human access or structural safety capability claimed or tested. No rigging, animation or interaction.
